newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-STROKE OF BAD LUCK DENIES UGANDANS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-STROKE OF BAD LUCK DENIES UGANDANS.

text.p: A double stroke of bad luck denied Uganda's only two entrants a chance to compete at the world short-course swimming championships.
Joy Nfashingabo, entered for the women's 50 and 100 metres events, missed her flight after she was robbed at Kampala airport, while breastroker Ismail Walusimbi got lost on the way to the pool.
Nfashingabo made the mistake of entrusting her travel funds to an unofficial moneychanger at Kampala airport.

"She waited and waited but he didn't turn up," said Walusimbi, who arrived safely in Gothenburg but got lost inside the competition venue and turned up too late to take part in his men's 100 metres breastroke heat on Friday.
Walusimbi, 17, did at least get into the water. He was allowed to swim alone in a timed trial of 100 metres, at the end of Friday morning's heats.
His time was one minute 34.59 seconds, which would have placed him last of 48 competitors in the heats. Germany's Jens Kruppa clocked the fastest time of one minute 00.37 seconds.
But Walusimbi and coach Suleiman Benwa said that just getting to the event was a victory of sorts.
"Our major aim was to take our swimmers and open them to the world scene, show them what it is like," Benwa said.
"Just the logistics of getting here, raising money from our families, getting here, surviving here, that saps you a lot."
